attempts.summary: Implemented sudo command logging on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, which has ansible-core installed). The playbook drops /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging setting `Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"`, `Defaults log_year`, `Defaults log_host`, and `Defaults !syslog`, and pre-creates the log file with 0600 root:root permissions. This makes sudo write every command (with user, host, timestamp, PWD, and COMMAND) directly to the dedicated file while suppressing sudo's normal syslog/authpriv output, keeping entries out of the general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified functionally with a real sudo invocation from a temporary test user, confirmed idempotence on replay, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for both node1 and node2, proving the configuration and log data survive a reboot and that sudo logging continues to work afterward with no new /var/log/secure entries.
